Set the rules once, then start the season
◆ YouYou run this league THE PRO
How serious is your league?
One pick, made now, that sets the fairness rules for the whole season — how much of your index you play off, how scores are vouched for, which courses count. Casual is an honor-system beer league. Standard asks you to post what you'd post to GHIN. Cutthroat wants receipts: vouched by the group where you can; the Pro rules on the rest. Deciding this before anyone tees off is what keeps October friendly.

Verification is a norm the league holds, not a filter the engine applies.

Buy-inPer player · $0 = bragging rights
None
OtherAny number, per player

Everyone who owes will see this. It's the only place they can look.

Season lengthWeeks or months · ends the same weekday
6 mo

First teePick any day
Teams
How the league is organized. Solo means everyone competes individually: no squads. Squad modes split the league into teams the Pro picks or draws; more squads want more players (4 squads plays best at 8+).

4 squads · the full cup experience for 8+ players.

How teams fill
How squads get filled. Random draw shuffles everyone server-side and announces the reveal to the board, so nobody can rig the hat. The Pro picks lets you place players yourself, for groups who picked teams in the group chat. Live picking with a clock isn't built yet.

Random draw: the server shuffles every joined player into squads and posts the reveal. Argument-proof.

How it ends
How the champion is crowned. Cup Final resets for the last four weeks — top seeds race fresh, anyone can catch fire, playoff drama. Points table crowns whoever leads when the season ends: the whole year is the race, no reset.

Cup Final: the last four weeks reset and score fresh — top seeds only, whoever's hottest takes the cup.

The pot split
How the pot pays out at season's end. Every split rewards the champion, the runner-up, and the Points King (best individual all year).

Balanced: champ 60% · runner-up 25% · Points King 15%.

Rounds that count Your best N each month score
Best 3
The dial that decides what a point means. Only your best N rounds each month score, so the retiree who plays daily can't bury the dad who plays weekly — and, just as much, so a good round is worth more than another round. Set it low and the table ranks how you played; set it high and it ranks how often you showed up. A better round always replaces your worst counter, so posting never stops mattering.
The monthly minimum ROUNDS A MONTH · −5 SQUAD POINTS SHORT
2 / mo
The anti-ghosting rule. Everyone posts at least this many rounds a month. Miss once and your season bye covers it automatically — no asking, no approval (D14); from the second miss the squad takes the penalty: −5 points per round short under Standard rules. Short months are waived.
